name: Collateral reduction without post-action solvency enforcement
description: A debt-bearing account can use a user-callable accounting or reserve-transfer path to reduce collateral backing without an equivalent post-action solvency check. An attacker who controls both the unhealthy account and a liquidator can then capture liquidation value that exceeds the economic cost of creating the unhealthy state.
structuralPreconditions: A protocol tracks collateral and debt in internal account state and exposes a user-callable path that can reduce collateral backing while debt remains outstanding.
The collateral-reducing path reaches committed accounting state without the same health or solvency enforcement applied to ordinary withdrawal or transfer paths.
The protocol exposes liquidation or equivalent unhealthy-position resolution that can transfer economically valuable assets or claims to a liquidator.
runtimePreconditions: The affected market or vault contains economically meaningful redeemable liquidity.
An attacker can create or obtain a debt-bearing position large enough that deliberately making it unhealthy can produce extractable liquidation value after costs.
attackerCapabilities: Control a debt-bearing account whose collateral can be reduced through the unchecked path.
Control or coordinate the liquidator side of the resulting unhealthy-position resolution.
Supply sufficient capital or temporary liquidity to create the economically meaningful position.
attackSequenceAbstract: Create or amplify a collateralized debt position.
Invoke the exceptional accounting, reserve-transfer, donation, or equivalent path that reduces collateral backing without equivalent post-action solvency enforcement.
Allow the deliberately unhealthy state to remain committed.
Liquidate or otherwise resolve the unhealthy account using an attacker-controlled counterparty.
Redeem or withdraw captured liquidation value and compare it with the cost of creating the unhealthy state.
expectedSecurityPropertyViolation: Every user action that materially reduces collateral backing outstanding debt must preserve required account solvency or revert before committing the unhealthy state.
An attacker must not be able to manufacture a net-profitable liquidation of an attacker-controlled account solely by exploiting inconsistent collateral-accounting enforcement.
sourceIntelligenceSignals: A public or externally reachable function can reduce collateral, reserves, shares, or equivalent backing for an account with outstanding debt.
The exceptional collateral-reducing path lacks a health-check call or bypasses a guard used by ordinary collateral-reducing paths.
A liquidation or bad-position settlement path transfers value to a caller or separately controlled account.
runtimeOverlaySignals: A probe shows that the candidate collateral-reducing action worsens account health while succeeding instead of reverting.
A subsequent attacker-controlled liquidation or settlement produces redeemable value that can be measured against the cost of the collateral reduction.
nonApplicabilitySignals: Every collateral-reducing path enforces an equivalent post-action health or solvency check before state is committed.
The candidate accounting or reserve-transfer path cannot reduce collateral that backs outstanding debt.
No attacker-controlled liquidation or settlement path can convert the deliberately unhealthy state into net extractable value.
The target's collateral conversion or liquidation accounting is isolated from the candidate state transition so the proposed sequence cannot change liquidation economics.
falsePositiveGuards: Do not classify a reserve or donation function as applicable unless it can actually make a debt-bearing account less healthy.
Do not infer missing solvency enforcement from function naming; verify the complete target call path and equivalent guards.
Do not treat a deliberately unhealthy state as exploitable unless an attacker-controlled liquidation or settlement can capture net value after the collateral-reduction loss and execution costs.
Do not transfer conclusions from one lending implementation to another unless source intelligence and runtime state independently satisfy the structural and runtime preconditions.
adaptationRules: Bind the generalized collateral-reducing action to the target-specific function or state transition identified by source intelligence rather than a historical function name.
Bind account-health observation to the target's canonical solvency, liquidity, collateral-ratio, or equivalent safety metric.
Bind liquidation/settlement and redemption to target-specific interfaces and measure attacker net value before and after the complete sequence.
Treat temporary liquidity as an amplifier, not a required root cause; run a smaller-capital variant when the target permits it.
limitations: Pattern similarity is not an exploitability judgment; target-specific source intelligence, runtime state, guards, and economics must be evaluated before scheduling an attack reproduction.
The pattern does not assume a particular lending protocol, contract address, function name, oracle, token, or historical block.
